newsitem.title: ITALY: INSTANT VIEW - Italy prelim Jan CPI 0.2 pct mo/mo.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Italy prelim Jan CPI 0.2 pct mo/mo.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the preliminary 0.2 percent month-on-month rise in Italian January consumer prices, released by 11 sample cities on Monday and Tuesday.
The year-on-year CPI rate was seen at 2.6 percent.

Economists in a Reuters survey on January 16 had forecast on average a month-on-month rate of 0.2 percent and a year-on-year rate of 2.6 percent. Analysts had seen a monthly rate of 0.1 percent and yearly gain of 2.5/2.6 percent after the first two cities, Trieste and Turin, released their data on Monday.
Pio De Gregorio, analyst at Natwest Capmarkets Milan said, "This is slightly better than expected. We could see inflation dropping to 2.0/2.1 percent by May or June if CPI continues to be benign."

De Gregorio said inflation on a monthly basis had edged up a bit but noted January usually is a strong month for consumer prices as it is the time when a whole range of public tariff rises come into effect.
But he said, "We could see inflation dropping to 2.0 or 2.1 percent by May or June if CPI continues to be benign."
He noted that there was a high basis of comparison given that CPI in the first months of 1996 was fairly strong, before slowing in the second half.
Lorenzo Stanca, head of research at Credito Italiano, forecast January CPI at 0.2 percent monthly and 2.6 percent year-on-year.

"This is an extremely good figure, it is good news. But the Bank of Italy looks at the medium to long term and will probably wait for an agreement in the metalworkers dispute before cutting interest rates," he said.

De Gregorio agreed. "I am confident that we should see a discount rate cut to 6.25 percent from the current 7.50 percent, with the Bank of Italy cutting by 50 basis points after an accord on pay contracts between the metalworkers and employers, and by a further 75 bps in the second quarter after an expected supplementary budget, or at least after this is announced."

"The inflation outlook is benign, but the Italian political situation is still muddled. The role and attitude of the marxist Communist Refoundation to Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government is the only question mark for the markets," De Gregorio added.
Lorenzo Codogno, head of research at Bank of America Milan, said he also forecast a monthly rate of 0.2 percent and annual figure of 2.6 percent.
"It is a positive result even if Monday's preliminary data had indicated a possibly even better result," he said.

Ilaria Fornari of J.P. Morgan said,"It is a very good figure. The seasonally-adjusted and annualised monthly variation over the last three months is on average 2.4 percent." -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
